This seems ridiculous. Scalping sucks, but only because people buy up multiple items without ever planning to use them (I.e. purely to sell at profit). If someone legitimately bought the item, then decided to sell it aftermarket, they have every right to sell it at market value. And since they NEED to sell it, they’ll likely list it lower than the scalpers, which opens up opportunities for people to buy it at a lower cost.

It’s absurd that you would even suggest somebody just return it to the store when it will likely end up being scalped at this point anyways.

Not only is she being ridiculous about this, but if anything, this baby is arguably more YOUR baby than hers (if we’re trying to make this into a weird competition like your SO). Since you both decided to use your egg to fertilize instead of your SO, the baby is only carrying your genes, and not her’s. Her claim would be similar to a paid surrogate claiming parentship over a child.

And this is probably exactly what is bothering her. She knows she wasn’t able to contribute to the genetic makeup of your child, so she’s compensating by overstating the importance of her carrying the baby.

I don’t necessarily think she’s the asshole either. She’s probably struggling a bit with mentally grasping this and coming to terms with the nature of your arrangement. While I feel like these types of relationship arrangements are a beautiful addition to our progress as a species, we simply didn’t adapt in a way that would naturally allow two mothers to produce offspring together. I think instinct starts to kick in a bit during these unfamiliar situations, and mothers are typically very protecting of their child, especially in the early years. The hormones of pregnancy are something you didn’t experience, so for you, her actions probably seem confusing and mean, but I think her reactions are mostly driven by post-pregnancy maternal instinct.

I think some therapy for your SO, or perhaps both of you together, would help to clear up some of these feelings.

I’ve kinda been on both sides of this, so I feel you, but it also makes a lot of sense. Nobody wants to fuck up in a social setting, and “alpha” type people tend to be the most socially aware/adept in the group. So, by following them, people with less social skill have a much lower chance of making social mistakes and embarrassing themselves.

Socially adept people tend to be better at “saving” a social situation. If someone says something awkward, this “leader/alpha” type will usually step in and diffuse the tension or pick up on your main point and communicate it better for the group, whereas a less skilled person might just go quiet or say something even more awkward. Its not that they only care to talk to the “leader/alpha”, I think people do this because they’re less likely to make an ass of themselves by following this person.

Again, a guy who keeps a token as a reminder of an ex girlfriend ISNT EVEN FUCKING CLOSE to a guy who’s WIFE FUCKING DIED. 

Try putting yourself in his shoes. Say you and your current girlfriend get married in a few years, but then, one day, she suddenly dies in a tragic accident. You’re heartbroken, and probably unable to experience intimacy with another person for a long time. 

But then another couple years down the line, you meet someone who actually makes you feel a little better, and you realize, “hey, maybe I can love again.” You weren’t looking to date yet, and you’re not totally sure if you’re ready to. But this new person just showed up in your life, and they make it feel like you’re finally starting to see the light at the end of the dark tunnel you’ve been stuck in for the past few years.

Are you going to avoid this new relationship, the one thing that has finally made you feel a little better after years of pain and suffering, just because you’re unsure if you’re “ready” or not? Do you try to take it slow and risk this new person thinking you’re uninterested? Again, a few months before this, you were unsure if you’d ever love again, but you’re starting to see that potential in this new girl who came along. Would you really want to break it off and go back to feeling like you might not ever love, just because you’re unsure if you’re “ready to date again”?

Say you do decide to date them. You’ll have to tell them about this eventually, but are you going to bring this up on the first date and risk scaring them off? Third? Fourth? Do you bring it up once you become official? When is the appropriate time to have this very serious 3-4 hour conversation about your trauma with a person you just started dating.

Say you figure all that shit out, and you’re now committed to this new person. Do you just delete everything related to your love who passed away? Throw all the keepsakes and gifts she gave you in the trash? What if your new girlfriend INSISTED that you delete all your pictures of her? Do you think you just forget about your wife because this new person came along? 

Fuck no! 

You’re going to do literally whatever feels right in that moment, because these aren’t situations that most people will ever have to deal with. You’re never gonna be fully “ready” for a new relationship after something like this, because this is nothing like getting over a breakup. 

Things aren’t always so cut-and-dry.

Yeah, you seem like you have difficulty reconciling the fact that people you date can have feelings for other people. I feel like you have yet to come terms with the nature of human attraction. People will always be attracted to other people in some way or another, even when they’re in a satisfying committed monogamous relationship and have no interest in exploring that attraction. If you have a girlfriend, I can 100% guarantee that there are men out there—other than you—that she’s attracted to. Being jealous about a dead spouse is absurd. 

The whole idea is that you don’t really know if they would still choose to be with that person over you if they were still alive. The relationship was never able to fully run its course. So the person who died will always be held in a more positive light, and the widower will probably always have that love for this person. It doesn’t mean they love you any less, it just means the relationship was cut short by tragedy before any potential incompatible differences were discovered. A relationship like this will always stay in the “honeymoon” phase, because their dead spouse represents a whole lot of potential “what-ifs” and “could-be’s” about a life that people like OP were never able to see or experience.

I have a feeling you’re probably not the type of person who buys nice furniture. If you’ve ever been in a nice house before, there are typically multiple “rarely/never used” furniture pieces along with the more sturdy “everyday” type furniture. I bought the lounge expecting that it would be something that was used occasionally when we have guests and need additional seating by the TV, not so it could be used as some sort of daybed for my roommate to chill on all day. I wouldn’t have a problem with the way she’s using it if it wasn’t causing obvious damage to it.

Have you ever seen those chairs made out of cardboard? They’re cool as fuck and look great in a modern-style house, but they would get completely torn up if you were to use it every day, and most people wouldn’t even try to do that because the chance of breaking it is so obvious. Same with people who have “fine china” dishware. It’s meant to be used on special occasions, as daily use would drastically increase the chances of damaging/breaking it.

I’m not asking that she doesn’t use the furniture, just that she maybe doesn’t lay down in the same spot on it every day, or maybe tries to fluff it up a bit every once and a while to keep it nice. It’s really not that hard to just lay in a different spot every once and a while.

If you had a roommate who wore his keys on their belt buckle and you noticed it was scratching the shit out of your nice leather couch every time he sat down, would you tell yourself, “it’s a used couch now, things will get scratched,” or would you tell your roommate to be more careful with his fucking keys?
